verdict.evidence:
The two blocks are algorithmically byte-identical. pruneEdgeProjectionCache (useTracing.ts:144-149) is `if (cache.size <= seenIds.size) return; for (const id of cache.keys()) if (!seenIds.has(id)) cache.delete(id)`. The inline node-cache prune (417-421) is `if (projectionCache.size > seenIds.size) { for (const id of projectionCache.keys()) if (!seenIds.has(id)) projectionCache.delete(id) }`. The guard `size <= seenIds.size -> return` is the exact logical inverse of `size > seenIds.size -> run loop`, and the deletion predicate (keys absent from seenIds) is the same.

Behavior trace, every case identical for inline vs a generic `pruneCacheBySeenIds<T>(cache: Map<string,T>, seenIds: Set<string>)`:
- Both seenIds sets are built identically (node loop line 361 adds every n.id; edge loops add every e.id). Cache and seenIds are both keyed by the same string ids, so sizes stay consistent.
- size > seenIds.size (extra cache keys): both prune all keys not in seenIds.
- size === seenIds.size but keys disjoint (node swapped for same-count node): inline guard false -> no prune; helper guard true -> return, no prune. Identical skip (pre-existing intentional optimization, leaves stale entry until a later pass; preserved exactly).
- empty seenIds, non-empty cache: both prune everything.
- Deleting from a Map while iterating its keys() is well-defined in JS (already-visited/current keys may be deleted safely); both forms do exactly this, so iteration order and final contents match. Retained projections keep reference identity (no entry is rewritten), so React Flow diff stability is unchanged.

Scope is NOT an obstacle: CachedProjection (342-351) is a function-local interface while CachedEdgeProjection (117-121) and the helper (144-149) are module-scope, but a module-scope generic over T only touches keys, never T's shape, so Map<string,CachedProjection> and Map<string,CachedEdgeProjection> are both assignable. The helper already serves 3 edge call sites (466, 507, 527); the node block (417-421) is the lone inlined holdout. Promoting pruneEdgeProjectionCache to the generic name backs all 4 sites with one body.

verdict.evidence:
FACTUAL CLAIM IS CORRECT. Effects fire in declaration order; the mount effect (CodeMirrorEditor.tsx:343) synchronously sets viewRef.current=view (line 453) before the [availableColumns] effect (line 474) runs, so on mount that effect dispatches columnCompartment.reconfigure() built from the same availableColumns prop -> a redundant transaction that lands the compartment in a functionally identical config. Behavior-preservation for the mount case holds: I verified @codemirror/autocomplete@6.20.1 -- autocompletion(config) returns module-level SINGLETONS (completionState StateField, completionPlugin, etc.) plus a fresh completionConfig.of(config). CodeMirror dedupes singletons by reference, so reconfiguring between two autocompletion() instances PRESERVES completionState (an open tooltip is not torn down); only the config facet (holding the override source) is swapped. The new closure columnCompletionSource(availableColumns) is built from the same array contents, so behavior is identical.

WHY ONLY MARGINAL, NOT SOUND: (1) The stated scope -- "~1 no-op transaction per mount" -- is a negligible micro-optimization; a compartment reconfigure with no doc/selection change triggers no content reflow and no completion recompute (sources only run on user interaction), so it is imperceptible and fixes no bug. (2) The candidate UNDER-SCOPES the real redundancy: at the RatingStepEditor.tsx:281 call site, codeAvailableColumns = Array.from(new Set([...])) is UNMEMOIZED -> a fresh array reference every parent render -> the [availableColumns] effect fires (and reconfigures) on EVERY RatingStepEditor re-render, not just at mount. (By contrast PolarsCodePanel.tsx:30 memoizes columnNames, so its reference is stable.) (3) The cheapest proposed fix (a didMount first-run guard) only suppresses the mount instance, leaving the per-render reconfigures, AND is risky here: main.tsx wraps the app in StrictMode (React 19.2.4) which double-invokes mount effects, and the mount effect itself creates a NEW EditorView on the second mount. There is already a regression test (_shared.test.tsx:438 "does not expose a destroyed stale editor view during StrictMode effect replay") proving this exact component has been bitten by StrictMode ordering. A first-run guard adds cross-effect ordering state that must stay correct across StrictMode replay, and it bakes in a silent-wrongness coupling (it assumes the mount effect always pre-installs the current columns) that violates the project's "fail loudly, no incorrect-and-hard-to-notice fallbacks" rule. The robust alternative (b) -- gate reconfigure on whether the column-set contents actually changed -- IS worthwhile and also kills the per-render churn, but it is addressing a larger problem than stated and is shifting work, not removing essential logic; the cleaner remedy is arguably to useMemo codeAvailableColumns at the call site rather than add guards inside the editor.

No net line reduction either way; this is a redundant-work cleanup, not a code-size simplification.

If this is pursued at all, prefer fixing the root cause at the call site: wrap codeAvailableColumns at RatingStepEditor.tsx:281 in useMemo (keyed on its inputs), which stabilizes the prop reference and naturally eliminates both the per-render reconfigures and (combined with the existing mount install) makes the mount reconfigure a true no-op-by-reference. Either way, gate any new logic behind a content-equality check (not a blind first-run skip) so a future refactor of mount/effect ordering fails loudly rather than silently serving stale completions. Low priority overall -- correctness is fine today; this is a minor perf hygiene item.

When the user clears the field (`e.target.value === ""`), it passes `undefined`, and `updateTermField` (lines 148-149: `if (value === undefined || value === null || value === "") delete updated[field]`) then REMOVES the `df` key. This is essential: `df` is optional for B-splines/nat-splines (TermSpec.df?: number, line 20), and clearing must drop the key so the backend uses its own default. The candidate proposes the shared `safeParseInt(raw, fallback)` and states it "avoids emitting NaN" by pinning a fallback. But `safeParseInt("", fallback)` returns the numeric fallback, never `undefined` — proven by the existing test configField.test.ts:83 `safeParseInt("", 7) === 7`. So the naive substitution never reaches the delete branch: clearing `df` would set it to a fallback number instead of removing it — a behavior change (bug). The radix justification is a false positive: `e.target.value` comes from `<input type="number">`, which only ever yields a valid decimal string or "" (never `0x...`), so `parseInt(value)` and `parseInt(value, 10)` are provably identical for every reachable value. The "consistency with sibling prior_weight (l.301)" argument is unsound because the inputs are not analogous: `prior_weight` always has a value, defaults to 1.0, and is never deleted (so safeParseFloat(value, 1.0) is correct there), whereas `df` is optional with delete-on-clear (so a safe-parse-with-fallback is the wrong idiom). A behavior-preserving variant must keep the guard (`e.target.value ? safeParseInt(e.target.value, ?) : undefined`), but inside the guard the input is non-empty and numeric, so safeParseInt never hits its fallback and never differs in radix — adding a meaningless fallback argument with zero behavioral change while inviting a future editor to "simplify" it into the broken form. The complexity is ESSENTIAL (encodes df optionality), not incidental.
verdict.est_reduction: ~1 line / consistency only — no real reduction; faithful version adds an inert argument rather than removing structure
verdict.recommended_action: Reject. Do not apply. The candidate as described (safeParseInt with fallback) silently changes the cleared-df behavior from "delete the df key" to "pin df to a fallback number", because safeParseInt('', fallback) returns the fallback, never undefined (verified by configField.test.ts:83). The radix "smell" is a lint false-positive for an `<input type="number">` (value can never be 0x-prefixed, so parseInt(v) === parseInt(v,10)). The asymmetry with the prior_weight sibling is intentional: df is optional/delete-on-clear, prior_weight is always-present/defaulted. Leave line 287 as-is. If churn-free idiom alignment is ever desired, only `e.target.value ? safeParseInt(e.target.value, NaN) : undefined` is faithful, but it provides no behavioral or readability benefit and raises future-edit risk — not worth it.

CURRENT MECHANISM (frontend/src/panels/editors/banding/BandingRulesGrid.tsx:200-216): ensureRuleIds() stamps a `_id` DATA PROPERTY onto rules; the no-dep effect writes the stamped rules back via onUpdateFactor exactly once per fresh rawRules identity (guarded by didAssignIds ref + the [rawRules] reset effect, which prevents an infinite render->update loop). A WeakMap keyed on identity misses and mints a new id, so the row's <tr key> changes, React unmounts/remounts the row and its focused <input>, dropping focus+caret after each character. Grep confirms this ladder exists ONLY in this component, so no other consumer can drift. CAVEAT 1 (concrete trap): the CSS-var families are NOT uniform — danger/success use `--{x}-soft`, `--{x}-border-strong`, `--{x}`, but the ACCENT border at line 225 is bare `1px solid var(--accent)`, NOT `var(--accent-border-strong)` (which does not exist; verified --accent-border-strong absent from index.css). So the fix must use an explicit per-variant style-map object; naive `--${variant}-border-strong` interpolation would emit an undefined CSS var for accent — a real regression. CAVEAT 2: the danger/success/accent decision also drives button *content* at lines 235-241, but that block orders `cache?.cached` BEFORE `hasStatusError`, the reverse of the style ladder, so it must NOT be folded into the same variant. CAVEAT 3: CacheFetchButton.test.tsx asserts only behavioral/stale-request concerns — no test reads the inline color/background/border values, so the visual mapping is unguarded and a careless refactor would pass CI silently. The simplification is sound in principle and behavior-preserving if done as a lookup table, but the benefit is genuinely small (~4 lines) against a concrete interpolation pitfall and zero test coverage on the mapping.
verdict.est_reduction: ~4 lines (accurate); removes 2 redundant evaluations of the variant predicate. Net small once a per-variant style-map object is introduced.
verdict.recommended_action: Optional cleanup, low priority. If taken: introduce a single `const variant = (building && cancelFetchFn) || hasStatusError ? 'danger' : cache?.cached ? 'success' : 'accent'` and an explicit per-variant style table (e.g. `{ danger: { background:'var(--danger-soft)', border:'1px solid var(--danger-border-strong)', color:'var(--danger)' }, success: {...}, accent: { background:'var(--accent-soft)', border:'1px solid var(--accent)', color:'var(--accent)' } }`) — do NOT use `--${variant}-border-strong` interpolation (accent has no such var). Leave the button-content branch (lines 235-241) untouched; its ordering differs. Reviewer should eyeball the three mappings since no test covers them.

verdict.evidence: File C:\Users\prici\haute\frontend\src\panels\explore\SchemaTableCard.tsx. nullSeverity (39-45) and nullPctStyle (57-63) compute the IDENTICAL expression pct=(nullCount/rowCount)*100 and branch on the IDENTICAL predicates in IDENTICAL order: rowCount===0, then pct>50, then pct===0, else default. Because pct is bit-for-bit identical in both, every input (nullCount,rowCount) always selects the same logical bucket in both functions; there is no input that lands in different buckets. Traced edge cases: rowCount===0 (both short-circuit before the division, so no NaN/Inf from 0/0); pct===0 is exactly equivalent to nullCount===0 in IEEE-754 (0/rowCount*100 is exactly 0; any nullCount>0 gives a strictly positive product), so strict float equality is safe and identical in both; pct>50 boundary identical. Both are pure (no side effects, no ordering concerns). A 4-bucket classifier classifyNullBucket -> 'empty'|'high'|'none'|'normal' is provably behavior-preserving when consumed as severity{empty->"none",high->"high",none->"none",normal->"normal"} and style{empty->MUTED_STYLE,high->warning-strong,none->MUTED_STYLE,normal->PRIMARY_STYLE} — note severity/style each collapse 'empty'+'none' to one output, so the 4 buckets map to 3 outputs; the consumer mappings reproduce that exactly. Existing test "marks null percentage severity buckets" (SchemaTableCard.test.tsx:187-217) pins the severity strings high/none/normal and would catch a regression; the colour ramp itself is NOT asserted in tests (only data-null-severity is), so a future threshold edit could TODAY silently desync colour from severity — unifying eliminates that latent bug, which is the genuine value. CAVEAT: formatNullPct is a SHARED util (frontend\src\utils\formatValue.ts:54) reused by ExploreSummaryCards.tsx:213,331 with its own test suite (formatValue.test.ts:180-189); it must NOT be folded in, and the proposed classifier (returns a bucket enum, not a percentage string) correctly leaves it untouched — so the "one of three redundant ratio computations removed" framing overstates the win: only the two local functions collapse, the percentage-string ratio stays.
verdict.est_reduction: Overstated by the candidate. Claimed ~10-14 lines + 1 of 3 ratio computations; realistic net is ~6-8 lines and only deduplicates the two LOCAL ratio/threshold ladders (formatNullPct's ratio must remain — it is a shared util). The classifier (~6 lines) plus two small bucket->severity and bucket->style mapping tables at the call site offset much of the gross saving; the durable benefit is the guaranteed colour/severity sync, not line count.
verdict.recommended_action: Apply: introduce a single pure classifyNullBucket(nullCount, rowCount): 'empty'|'high'|'none'|'normal' in SchemaTableCard.tsx, and derive both the data-null-severity string and the style object from it via explicit mapping (empty/none -> "none"/MUTED_STYLE, high -> "high"/warning-strong, normal -> "normal"/PRIMARY_STYLE). Keep formatNullPct unchanged (shared util, separate tests). Keep the existing severity test; additionally add an assertion on the rendered null-% cell colour for the high bucket so colour desync is caught going forward. Correct the est_reduction to ~6-8 lines and drop the "third ratio computation" claim in the tracking record.

The parent ModellingConfig.tsx:118 uses a DIFFERENT predicate (`... && !exclude.includes(c.name)`) and `.length` not `.map`, across a props boundary, to compute the `featureCount` prop.
